bias.headline: Conditions are modestly bullish (led by Volatility). This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBullish.label: Volatility
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBullish.explanation: SPY typically moves 0.81% in a day right now — more volatile than 10% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 10% of them

topBullish.label: Risk Appetite
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 69th percentile.
topBullish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are beating safe government bonds by 2.0% — money is willing to take risk to earn more, which usually accompanies a rising stock market.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 69% of them

topBullish.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing low held; no structural break below 752.18
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 10 swing highs and 10 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 12% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
topBullish.explanation: SPY is printing higher highs and higher lows — an intact uptrend. Last swing high 779.09 vs prior 773.50; last swing low 762.63 vs prior 752.18.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
topBullish.nextTrigger: breaks down below the last swing low of 762.63

topBearish.label: Market Breadth
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
topBearish.explanation: 34% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 17% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 59%.
topBearish.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 17% of them

watchNext.label: Trend Strength
watchNext.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.15 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.

conflicts: Net move is positive but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.15 now

metrics.explanation: Over the last 60 trading days IWM is 10.2% behind the S&P 500. That is a wider gap than 1% of the readings in its own history against the index — so this is unusually weak for this name.
metrics.whyItMatters: An instrument that persistently lags its benchmark is not participating in the move, whatever its own chart says. Relative strength separates a rising tide from genuine demand.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 1% of them

metrics.label: Market Breadth
metrics.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
metrics.explanation: 34% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 17% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 59%.
metrics.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 17% of them

metrics.label: Trend Strength
metrics.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.13 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions IWM moved -5.2%, and only 13% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.13 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing high rejected; no reclaim above 287.21
metrics.confidenceBasis: 12 swing highs and 9 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 13% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: IWM is printing lower highs and lower lows — an intact downtrend. Last swing high 283.38 vs prior 287.21; last swing low 277.89 vs prior 283.92.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
metrics.nextTrigger: breaks up above the last swing high of 283.38

metrics.label: Risk Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 69th percentile.
metrics.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are beating safe government bonds by 2.0% — money is willing to take risk to earn more, which usually accompanies a rising stock market.
metrics.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.24% in a day right now — more volatile than 6% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 6% of them
